doc.name: A — auto parts catalogue, backlit silhouette, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: drilled brake disc and pad set
Category: auto parts
Shot programme: backlit silhouette
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You act as lead photographer and set designer for an auto parts catalogue. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the low-angle monument in a backlit silhouette treatment.

SUBJECT. A drilled brake disc and pad set. The reference image governs silhouette, material finish and every printed mark. Reproduce the label text exactly as it appears; never invent new copy, logos or claims.

CAMERA. Low angle looking up so the product reads as architecture against the backdrop. Shoot on a 28mm at f/8, framing for leading lines converging on the subject from the lower corners.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with blue-hour ambient with a single warm practical for separation. Stage the product on or against ribbed fluted glass, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a sun-bleached grade with faded blacks and a green-yellow bias. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
